examples.en: My friend called me out of the blue.
Tears came out of nowhere, and I was flustered.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 뜬금없이 노래를 부르면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are you doing, singing out of the blue in the middle of a meeting?
My younger sibling suddenly suggested going on a trip.
An old song popped into my head out of nowhere.

examples.ko: 그는 뜬금없이 나타나서 선물을 주고 갔어요.
examples.en: He showed up out of nowhere, gave me a gift, and left.

explain: '갑자기'는 단순히 급하게 일어난 일을 말하고, '뜬금없이'는 앞뒤 흐름과 맞지 않아서 어리둥절한 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '뜬금없는 소리', '뜬금없이 왜 그래?'처럼 써요. 대화에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Don't say such random things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞뒤가 맞지 않는 말을 할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for a remark that comes from nowhere.

phrases.en: He suddenly started laughing for no reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 알 수 없는 행동에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits actions with no clear reason.
phrases.en_equiv: to laugh out of the blue

phrases.en: It suddenly started to rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단순히 급하게 일어난 일에 써서 '뜬금없이'보다 어리둥절한 느낌이 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Just means suddenly, without the baffled feel of 뜬금없이.

explain_en: 갑자기 just means something happened suddenly, while 뜬금없이 adds a feeling of confusion because it does not fit the flow. It is common in phrases like 뜬금없는 소리 or 뜬금없이 왜 그래?. You will hear it a lot in conversation.

examples.en: Where is the bottle opener?
Please open the cola cap with the bottle opener.
I put a bottle opener in my camping bag.
I didn't have a bottle opener, so I opened it with a spoon.
This key ring can also be used as a bottle opener.
If you open the drawer, there are a bottle opener and scissors.

explain: 주로 병뚜껑을 따는 도구예요. 캔을 따는 도구는 '캔따개', 코르크를 여는 도구는 '와인오프너'라고 구분해서 말해요.

phrases.en: I borrowed a bottle opener from the neighbors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 도구를 잠깐 쓸 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for temporarily using a tool you need.

phrases.en: I didn't have a bottle opener, so I opened it with a spoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구가 없는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing a situation without the tool.
phrases.en_equiv: to not have a bottle opener

phrases.en: When I opened the bottle cap, foam came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병따개로 하는 일을 직접 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Directly describes the action done with a bottle opener.

explain_en: It is mainly the tool for opening bottle caps. A tool for cans is called '캔따개', and one for corks is a '와인오프너'.

examples.ko: 시험 때마다 불안증이 심해져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My anxiety gets worse every exam, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 불안증 때문에 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: Because of my anxiety, I can't sleep well at night.
He has suffered from anxiety for a long time.

examples.ko: 운동을 하면 불안증이 조금 나아지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Exercising seems to ease my anxiety a little.

examples.ko: 불안증이 있는 친구에게는 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak slowly to a friend who has anxiety.

examples.ko: 요즘 불안증으로 상담을 받는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days many people get counseling for anxiety.

explain: '불안'은 누구나 느끼는 기분이고, '불안증'은 그 기분이 오래가서 생활이 힘들 정도인 증상을 말해요. 병원이나 상담 이야기에서 '불안증이 있다/심하다/생기다'처럼 써요. 가벼운 기분은 그냥 '불안해요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 큰 사고를 겪은 뒤에 불안증이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: After going through a serious accident, I developed anxiety.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 겪은 뒤 증상이 시작될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the symptoms begin after some experience.

phrases.en: He suffered from anxiety for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 증상을 오래 경험했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means going through the hard symptoms for a long time.

phrases.en: I got treatment for anxiety and improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 상담에서 증상을 낫게 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to getting treatment at a hospital or counseling.

explain_en: '불안' is a feeling anyone can have, while '불안증' is a lasting condition that makes daily life hard. It appears in talk about hospitals and counseling, as in '불안증이 있다/심하다/생기다'. For a mild feeling, just say '불안해요'.

t90.ax: He has suffered from anxiety for a long time.

examples.ko: 어, 이거 왜 생사람을 끌고 들어가요?
examples.en: Hey, why are you dragging an innocent person into this?
Don't accuse an innocent person without any evidence.

examples.ko: 저는 아무것도 안 했는데 생사람이 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: I didn't do anything, but I feel like I've been made out to be guilty.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제가 한 게 아니에요. 생사람에게 누명을 씌우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: I didn't do that. You can't frame an innocent person.

examples.ko: 오해 때문에 생사람 하나가 의심을 받았어요.
examples.en: Because of a misunderstanding, an innocent person came under suspicion.
I want to clear the grievance of an innocent person.

explain: 아무 잘못이 없는데 의심받거나 혼나는 사람을 말하고, 대부분 '생사람 잡다'라는 표현으로 나와요. '누명', '억울하다'와 같이 쓰이는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 저는 안 했는데 왜 생사람 잡아요?
phrases.en: I didn't do it, so why are you blaming me?
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이 없는 사람을 잘못했다고 몰아붙인다는 말이에요. 억울해서 항의할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means pinning blame on someone who did nothing wrong. It is used in a tone of protest when you feel wronged.

explain_en: It refers to a person who has done nothing wrong yet is suspected or scolded, and it mostly appears in the expression '생사람 잡다'. It is often used together with words like '누명' (a false charge) and '억울하다' (feel wronged).

examples.en: I'm a light eater, so one bowl is enough.
When I eat with a friend who eats little, food gets left over.

examples.ko: 우리 할머니는 소식가셔서 늘 조금만 드세요.
examples.en: My grandmother is a light eater, so she always eats just a little.
I naturally eat little, so buffets aren't great for me.
You eat so little. You're really a light eater.
My husband is a light eater, but he's very healthy.

explain: 반대말은 많이 먹는 사람을 뜻하는 '대식가'예요. 사람을 가리킬 때는 '소식가'를 쓰고, 적게 먹는 행동은 '소식하다'라고 해요. 보통 '저는 소식가예요'처럼 자기 식사량을 설명할 때 써요.

phrases.en: For my health, I eat lightly in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 적게 먹는 행동을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb for the act of eating little, not for the person.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 대식가라서 밥을 세 그릇 먹어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is a big eater and eats three bowls of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소식가'의 반대말로 많이 먹는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 소식가; a person who eats a lot.

phrases.en: I'm naturally on the light-eating side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편이다'를 붙이면 단정하지 않고 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 편이다 softens the statement instead of stating it flatly.
phrases.en_equiv: tend to be a light eater

explain_en: The opposite is '대식가', a big eater. Use '소식가' for the person, and '소식하다' for the act of eating little. It is typically used to describe your own appetite, as in '저는 소식가예요'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 속사포처럼 말해서 알아듣기 힘들어요.
examples.en: He talks like a machine gun, so he is hard to understand.
The rapper rattled off a rapid-fire rap.
My younger sibling fired off questions one after another.
I was overwhelmed by the rapid-fire nagging.
When I'm nervous in an interview, I end up talking really fast.

examples.ko: 속사포로 설명하지 말고 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't explain at breakneck speed; speak slowly.

explain: 원래는 빠르게 연속으로 쏘는 대포를 말하지만, 지금은 말이 아주 빠르거나 질문, 잔소리가 쏟아지는 모습에 '속사포처럼'으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: to talk at lightning speed
phrases.nuance_ko: 총을 연속으로 쏘듯 말이 쉴 새 없이 빠르게 나오는 모습이에요. 듣는 사람이 따라가기 힘들다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Words come out nonstop like rapid gunfire, with the feeling that the listener can hardly keep up.

explain_en: It originally refers to a quick-firing gun, but now it is mostly used as '속사포처럼' for very fast speech or a flood of questions and nagging.

examples.ko: 망명을 받아 주는 나라가 없으면 신변이 위험해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If no country accepts their asylum, their personal safety could be at risk.
The police are protecting the witness's personal safety.

examples.ko: 요즘 신변에 이상한 일이 생기지 않았나요?
examples.en: Hasn't anything strange happened around you lately?

examples.ko: 혼자 사는 사람은 신변 안전에 더 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: People who live alone should pay more attention to their personal safety.

examples.ko: 그는 신변의 위협을 느껴서 이사를 갔어요.
examples.en: He felt his safety was threatened, so he moved away.

examples.ko: 연예인은 신변 보호를 위해 경호원을 둬요.
examples.en: Celebrities hire bodyguards for their personal protection.

explain: 몸 자체보다 '몸과 목숨, 안전, 주변 일'을 가리켜요. '신변 보호', '신변 안전', '신변이 위험하다'처럼 굳은 짝으로 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '안전'이나 '몸'으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 피해자에게 신변 보호를 해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The police provided protection to the victim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 사람의 안전을 지켜 주는 일을 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to guarding the safety of someone in danger; common in the news.

phrases.example: 여행 중에는 신변 안전에 신경 쓰세요.
phrases.en: Pay attention to your personal safety while traveling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신의 몸과 목숨의 안전을 말할 때 쓰는 굳은 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed pairing for the safety of one's body and life.

phrases.en: I received threats, so my safety is at risk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 일이 닥칠 수 있다는 걱정을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express worry that something dangerous could happen.

explain_en: Rather than the physical body itself, it refers to one's person, life, safety and personal surroundings. It is mostly used in set phrases like '신변 보호', '신변 안전', and '신변이 위험하다'. It appears often in the news, while daily talk uses '안전' or '몸'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 수비하다가 갑자기 역습해서 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team was defending, then suddenly counterattacked and scored a goal.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 역습하기 전에 수비를 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to organize our defense before the other team counterattacks.
In the second half we counterattacked quickly.

examples.ko: 약해 보여도 기회가 오면 역습할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if we look weak, we can strike back when a chance comes.
The players ran out to counterattack as soon as they won the ball.

examples.ko: 앞서던 팀이 방심한 사이에 상대가 역습하네요.
examples.en: While the leading team let its guard down, the opponent is counterattacking.

explain: 축구 같은 스포츠 중계에서 공을 빼앗고 곧바로 공격에 나서는 상황에 가장 많이 나와요. '반격하다'와 비슷하지만, 말싸움처럼 넓은 경우에는 '반격하다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요. 역습은 빠르게 되받아치는 공격에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 공을 뺏자마자 우리 팀이 역습에 나섰어요.
phrases.en: As soon as we won the ball, our team launched a counterattack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '역습'을 써서 반격을 시작한다는 뜻으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 역습 to say a team starts a counterattack.

phrases.example: 공격하다가 갑자기 역습을 당해서 한 골을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: We were hit by a sudden counterattack while attacking and conceded a goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '역습하다'와 반대로 내가 상대의 역습을 받는 경우에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite perspective: you are the one on the receiving end of a counterattack.

phrases.example: 상대가 세게 공격했지만 우리도 바로 반격했어요.
phrases.en: The opponent attacked hard, but we hit back right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠뿐 아니라 말싸움처럼 넓은 상황에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works beyond sports, including arguments and other situations.

explain_en: It appears most in sports commentary such as soccer, when a team wins the ball and attacks right away. It is similar to '반격하다', but for broader cases such as arguments '반격하다' sounds more natural. '역습하다' suits a fast strike back.

examples.en: I scrunched up my face after eating something spicy.

examples.ko: 아침부터 오만상을 찌푸리고 있어요? 무슨 일 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you scowling since this morning? Did something happen?
The smell was so bad that everyone made a sour face.
Don't scowl; talk with a smile.
He grimaced when he saw his test score.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 오만상을 찌푸리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't scowl when you take a photo.

explain: '인상을 쓰다'와 비슷한 상황에서 쓰는데, 얼굴을 한껏 찡그린 모습을 강조해요. 보통 '오만상을 찌푸리다'로 말하고 표정에만 써요.

phrases.en: I scowled after taking the bitter medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찌푸리다' 대신 '쓰다'를 써도 얼굴을 심하게 찡그린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 'to put on' instead of 'to furrow' still means a deep scowl.

phrases.en: I drank the medicine with a deep scowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형이라서 찡그린 얼굴로 다른 행동을 했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connective form, for doing something while scowling.

phrases.en: Don't frown; try smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오만상'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday expression than the headword.

explain_en: It is used in situations similar to '인상을 쓰다' but stresses a face scrunched up a lot. It usually appears as '오만상을 찌푸리다' and is only used for facial expressions.

examples.en: The boss threatened us to finish it by today.
The older brother made a threat to his younger brother.

examples.ko: 아무리 으름장을 놓아도 아이는 겁먹지 않았어요.
examples.en: No matter how much I threatened him, the child wasn't scared.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 으름장 때문에 모두 입을 다물었어요.
examples.en: Everyone kept quiet because of his threats.

examples.ko: 으름장만 놓고 실제로 한 건 없어요.
examples.en: He only makes threats and has never actually done anything.

examples.ko: 빨리 안 나가면 혼난다는 으름장에 아이들이 도망갔어요.
examples.en: The kids ran away at the warning that they'd be in trouble if they didn't leave.

explain: 보통 '으름장을 놓다'로 써요. 말로 겁을 줘서 상대가 뜻대로 하게 하려는 느낌이고, '협박'보다 가볍게 들릴 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 숙제를 안 하면 혼난다고 엄포를 놓으셨어요.
phrases.en: The teacher threatened that we'd be in trouble if we didn't do our homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으름장을 놓다'와 비슷하게, 겁을 주려고 큰소리치는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 으름장을 놓다: talking big to scare someone.

phrases.example: 아이가 형의 으름장에 겁을 먹고 울었어요.
phrases.en: The child got scared by his older brother's threats and cried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 으름장을 들은 사람의 반응을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the reaction of the person who hears the threat.
phrases.en_equiv: to be scared by a threat

phrases.en: Don't try to threaten me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반말로 상대에게 겁주지 말라고 할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual-speech way to tell someone to stop trying to scare you.

explain_en: It is usually used as '으름장을 놓다'. It means scaring someone with words to make them do what you want, and it often sounds lighter than '협박' (a serious threat).

en: to torture oneself; to be cruel to oneself

examples.en: Don't be too hard on yourself just because you made a mistake.

examples.ko: 그는 시험에 떨어지고 며칠 동안 자학했어요.
examples.en: He beat himself up for days after failing the exam.
There's no need to torment yourself. Everyone fails.

examples.ko: 스스로를 자학하는 습관은 마음 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The habit of putting yourself down is bad for your mental health.
My friend cried, putting herself down and saying she was worthless.
Beating yourself up won't change anything.

explain: '자책하다'는 자기 잘못을 탓하는 것이고, '자학하다'는 스스로를 깎아내리고 괴롭히는 느낌이 더 세요. 보통 '자학하지 마세요'처럼 위로하거나 말릴 때 많이 써요. 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말은 '스스로를 괴롭히다'예요.

phrases.en: He often makes self-deprecating jokes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 깎아내리는 말이나 태도를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe words or attitudes that put oneself down.

phrases.en: Don't be so hard on yourself; take a rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들어하는 사람을 위로하거나 말릴 때 가장 많이 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used to comfort or stop someone who is being hard on themselves.
phrases.en_equiv: don't be so hard on yourself

phrases.en: Don't torment yourself alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자학하다'와 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing as '자학하다'.

explain_en: '자책하다' is blaming yourself for a fault, while '자학하다' feels stronger, like belittling and tormenting yourself. It is often used to comfort or stop someone, as in '자학하지 마세요'. A plainer way to say it is '스스로를 괴롭히다'.

examples.en: My friend who was on leave re-enrolled this spring.

examples.ko: 재입학 신청은 다음 주까지 해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to apply for re-admission by next week.

examples.ko: 학교를 그만둔 지 오 년 만에 재입학을 결심했어요.
examples.en: Five years after leaving school, I decided to go back.
What documents do I need if I want to re-enroll?
After re-entering, my younger sibling changed majors.
I heard the re-entrance exam isn't hard.

explain: 학교를 그만둔 뒤 같은 학교에 다시 입학하는 것을 말해요. 휴학했다가 돌아오는 '복학'과는 달라요. 다른 학교의 학년으로 들어가는 '편입'과도 구별해서 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 내년에 같은 학교에 재입학하려고 해요.
phrases.en: I plan to re-enroll in the same school next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '재입학'을 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 재입학.

phrases.en: The school gave permission to re-enroll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교가 다시 받아 주는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the school approves re-entry.

phrases.en: I quit school and then enrolled again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say it.

explain_en: It means entering the same school again after having left it. It differs from '복학', which is coming back after a leave of absence. It is also distinct from '편입', which means transferring into another school.
